newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Renewed U.S. interest rate jitters triggered a sharp fall in U.S. Treasury bond prices which spilled over into the local gilt market and pushed yields to a critical technical juncture late on Friday, dealers said.
At 1400 GMT, the key R150 was pegged at a 15.29 percent yield from 15.22 percent on Thursday after having languished for much of the day between 15.20 and 15.26 percent in exceptionally dull trade.

In early New York trade, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond kicked up to a 7.18 percent yield from 7.10 percent overnight in the wake of U.S. March PPI and retail sales which dealers said increased the prospect of a Fed tightening in the near future.
While overall U.S. PPI was flat in the month, falling 0.1 percent month-on-month, the market focussed on the core rate which rose 0.4 percent from February.

U.S. retail sales came in below expectations with a 0.2 percent rise. But that came after a sharp upward revision in February and January sales to 1.5 and 1.7 percent respectively from preliminary 0.8 and 1.5 percent increases.

Local traders said the data had renewed fears that the Federal Reserve would hike interest rates by a further 25 basis points at its next Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20, duplicating a move by the Fed on March 25.
The selloff on the U.S. market prompted heavy selling shortly after the data's release at 1230 GMT, pushing the R150 to 15.29 percent -- a key technical level.
"15.29 is a double top, which is technically a crucial level. If it breaks we will be in a full blown bear market," a trader said, adding that the next target on the upside would be the 15.40 area.
But traders said the U.S. market was already looking toppish at the 7.18 percent level and the local market should retrace early next week to around the 15.24 percent level.
"I wouldn't be surprised if we pull back from these levels," a trader said. "The market seems to want to hold these levels."
On the currency market, the rand staged something of a recovery after initially attempting to move back above the 4.46 level on speculative dollar demand out of London.
The rand was last quoted at 4.4530/4560 against the dollar from 4.4580/4610 overnight.

Initially, the speculative buying pushed the rand to its day's weakest level of 4.46 bid, before a local export order to sell dollars, said by dealers to be in the region of $100 million, helped the currency retrace some lost ground.
Dealers said the currency met technical resistance as well as importer demand for dollars below the 4.45 level, which brought it back to its 1400 GMT level.
Next week, dealers said the rand was expected to hold a 4.45 to 4.47 range, although much would depend on the dollar's performance over the weekend.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 28.2963/3506 yen, 0.3868/3874 marks and 7.2321/2447 rand against sterling.

On the money market, three-month deposit rates were quoted unchanged in a 16.60 to 16.65 percent offered range, while the 90-day BA rate was slightly lower at between 15.95 and 16.10 percent from 15.95 to 16.15 percent on Thursday.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage rose to 8.780 billion rand on Thursday from 8.161 billion rand on Wednesday.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 199.17 million rand's worth of South African bonds after selling 126.18 million rand's worth on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 35.91 billion rand on Thursday -- settlement day -- from 5.25 billion rand previously.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
